target.title: fix(plugin-sdk): keep approval slugs UTF-16-safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Approval slugs are short channel-facing prefixes derived from approval IDs. Several builders produced them with `id.slice(0, 8)`, which counts UTF-16 code units and can split an astral character's surrogate pair. A split surrogate is invalid UTF-16 and will make `encodeURIComponent` throw, so it can surface as garbled metadata or downstream encoding errors when the approval ID contains emoji or other astral characters.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replaced the raw `slice(0, 8)` calls with `truncateUtf16Safe(..., 8)`, the existing surrogate-aware helper from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`. This keeps the same 8-character budget while refusing to cut a surrogate pair in half.

## User Impact

Approval prompts and reaction metadata that derive slugs from plugin/exec approval IDs now stay well-formed when the ID lands on a surrogate boundary.

## Evidence

- `src/plugin-sdk/approval-renderers.ts`: `buildPluginApprovalPendingReplyPayload`, `buildTypedPluginApprovalPendingReplyPayload`, and `buildPluginApprovalResolvedReplyPayload` now truncate with `truncateUtf16Safe`.
- `src/plugin-sdk/approval-reaction-runtime.ts`: `buildMetadataPayload` and the exec fallback in `buildApprovalReactionPendingContent` now truncate with `truncateUtf16Safe`.
- Regression tests in `approval-renderers.test.ts` and `approval-reaction-runtime.test.ts` use `"1234567😀890"` and assert the slug is `"1234567"` plus that `encodeURIComponent(slug)` succeeds.

## Real behavior proof

- Test command:
  ```bash
  pnpm test src/plugin-sdk/approval-renderers.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/approval-reaction-runtime.test.ts
  ```
- Output:
  ```
   Test Files  2 passed (2)
        Tests  25 passed (25)
     Duration  4.01s
  ```
- Before behavior: `"1234567😀890".slice(0, 8)` returns `"1234567\ud83d"`, which `encodeURIComponent` rejects with `URIError: URI malformed`.
- After behavior: `truncateUtf16Safe("1234567😀890", 8)` returns `"1234567"`, and `encodeURIComponent` succeeds.
